items.prompt: Two tabs load revision 0. Tab A saves and releases the Web Lock; tab B then acquires it with a draft based on revision 0. What stops B from overwriting A's change?
items.answer: Inside the lock, save compares the current stored text with the exact raw text remembered when B's draft began, and throws a conflict because they differ
distractors: The Web Lock itself refuses B because A held it more recently
B's revision number 0 is lower than storage's, so validateState rejects it
Nothing; the last tab to save wins, which is the documented behavior
items.explanation: A lock serializes cooperating saves but does not know what each draft was based on; the baseline comparison (compare-and-set) does.

items.prompt: Another tool rewrites the storage key with the same revision number but different content. Does a draft started before that write still save?
items.answer: No - the comparison is on the raw string, so any change at all, even one leaving revision unchanged, makes the baseline stale
distractors: Yes - only the revision number is compared
Yes - parsed objects are deep-compared and the categories are merged
Only if the other tool also held the Web Lock
items.explanation: Comparing raw text rather than a parsed field means no write can slip past the check by preserving one number.

items.prompt: An imported board file claims revision: 999 and is saved onto empty storage. What revision is committed?
items.answer: 1 - the next revision is computed from current storage plus one, and the spread overwrites the candidate's revision
distractors: 999, because validateState accepts any safe integer revision
1000, the imported revision plus one
0, because imported files always reset the revision
items.explanation: Revision is derived, not trusted: { ...normalized, revision: revision + 1 }.

items.prompt: setItem throws because storage is full while the learner saves an edited board. What does the learner see?
items.answer: An error, with the proposal still visible in the dialog and the accepted board unchanged, because current is replaced only after store.save succeeds
distractors: The edited board, which disappears on the next reload
An empty board, since the failed write cleared the key
The edited board, saved to sessionStorage as a fallback
items.explanation: A draft is a proposal; the saved board is accepted state. Updating the screen before persistence succeeds is the classic CRUD bug this avoids.

items.prompt: The learner deletes a question that was already marked used. What happens to usedQuestionIds?
items.answer: removeQuestion filters out exactly that id, and the other markers still point at the right tiles because they store question ids, not positions
distractors: Every marker shifts down one position to follow the array
The markers are kept, and validation later repairs them
All used markers are cleared to avoid inconsistent state
items.explanation: Stable ids distinguish records from positions, so deleting the first question cannot make its marker refer to the former second question.

items.prompt: An imported board gives a category and one of its questions the same id 'x'. Does validateState accept it?
items.answer: No - categories and questions are claimed through one shared set, so the second 'x' throws 'Duplicate record identity.'
distractors: Yes - category ids and question ids live in separate namespaces
Yes - only question ids need to be unique
No - but only because 'x' is shorter than the minimum id length
items.explanation: One claim() set covers both record kinds, so an id is unique across the whole board.

items.prompt: The stored board is malformed JSON. What does the app do on load?
items.answer: parseState throws, valid becomes false, the raw text is kept for download, and the examples render with tiles and editing disabled
distractors: It silently overwrites the key with the example board
It deletes the corrupt key and starts with an empty bank
It crashes with an uncaught SyntaxError and a blank page
items.explanation: Nothing is written until the user explicitly chooses replacement, and the raw text can be exported first.

items.prompt: With replaceInvalid: true, which check is excused - and which still runs?
items.answer: Only parsing the corrupt current value is excused; the baseline comparison still runs first, so an old recovery screen cannot overwrite a newer repair
distractors: Both the baseline comparison and the parse are skipped
Validation of the candidate is skipped so examples always save
The Web Lock is skipped because recovery is single-tab
items.explanation: Recovery refuses to overwrite unreadable data without both confirmation and a matching baseline.

items.prompt: A category name contains . Validation accepts it. Why does it not execute?
items.answer: The renderer sets textContent, so the value is displayed as literal text and never parsed as HTML
distractors: validateState strips angle brackets from every name
The CSP blocks the image from loading, so onerror never fires
Browsers never execute event handlers inside h2 elements
items.explanation: Validation and safe rendering are different defences; the CSP is a second layer, not the primary one.

items.prompt: The learner double-clicks Save. What prevents a second concurrent save?
items.answer: The first click disables every control, so the second lands on a disabled button; if (busy) return false is defence in depth for programmatic calls
distractors: The Web Lock queues the second save, which then conflicts
The browser debounces double-clicks on buttons automatically
Nothing; both saves run and the second overwrites the first
items.explanation: The ignored attempt shows no message - finding 6 notes this silent no-op could confuse a future caller.

items.prompt: A clue dialog is open when another tab starts a new round. The learner clicks Mark used. What happens?
items.answer: The save is checked against clue.raw captured when the dialog opened, so it conflicts with 'This board changed in another tab' - safe but conservative
distractors: The clue is marked used and the other tab's new round is lost
The clue is marked used on top of the new round automatically
The dialog closes silently without saving anything
items.explanation: It cannot resurrect old progress, but the user must close and reopen the clue; rebasing compatible changes would need its own test.

items.prompt: Is the answer secret until the learner clicks 'Reveal answer'?
items.answer: No - showClue writes question.answer into a hidden element, so anyone with devtools can read it; hidden is presentation, not secrecy
distractors: Yes - the answer is fetched from the server only on reveal
Yes - the answer is encrypted in storage until revealed
Yes - the CSP blocks devtools from reading hidden elements
items.explanation: Fine for a local study tool; any multi-user version must omit protected fields from what it sends.

items.front: Which invariant must survive any framework change in front of BoardStore (test/store.test.js:106-119)?
items.back: Two cooperating savers sharing one baseline produce exactly one winner and one revision: Promise.allSettled shows 1 fulfilled and 1 rejected save, and the stored revision is 1.

items.front: In BoardStore.save (store.js:51-59), what does deleting line 53 break, and why would removing the lock on line 51 instead still leave a window?
items.back: Without line 53 (the baseline compare) tab B overwrites tab A. Without the lock, lines 52-59 still run uninterrupted within one tab (no await), but tabs may run in separate processes and localStorage has no atomic read-modify-write across them, so two compare-then-write sequences can interleave.

items.front: store.js:53 compares the whole serialized board. Why should a reviewer not flag 'two tabs editing different questions conflict' as a bug?
items.back: Whole-board CAS is coarse by design and documented as a limit. Fixing it needs per-record versions (e.g. a server database with conditional updates), which is a later exercise - not a tweak to this comparison.

items.front: Senior-review finding 1: validation in store.js:20-21 throws 'Points must be...' or 'Prompt must contain...'. What is missing and how would you fix it?
items.back: The message does not identify the record, so repairing a 2 MiB import means hunting. The validator already has category and question indices in scope inside its map callbacks; include them (and the category name) in the thrown message.
